question: The correct increasing order of metallic character is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ge Ga Sc Ca**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ge and Ga **are in the same period (4), with Ga to the left of Ge.**
 
• Thus, Ga is more metallic than Ge.
 
• **Sc and Ca are also in period 4**. 
 
• Ca is to the left of Sc, **so Ca is more metallic than Sc.**
 
• Ga and Ge are in group 13 and 14 respectively whereas Sc and Ca are in group 3 and 2 respectively.
 
• Elements of group 2 are more metallic than group 3, which are more metallic than group 13 and 14.
 
• Thus, **both Ca and Sc are more metallic than Ga and Ge.**
 
• Ge 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The periodic table accommodates a discrete combination of metal, non-metals, and metalloids.
 
• The metallic character increases down the group. 
 
• On moving from left to right in a period, the electrons are added into the same valence shell progressively.
 
• The increase in the number of electrons is paralleled by the increase in the number of protons in the nucleus.
 
• The effective nuclear charge is increased and the valence shell electrons are pulled strongly by electrostatic attraction.
 
• Therefore, it is difficult to give away the valence electrons, the electropositivity is decreased and so the metallic character is also decreased.
 
• On moving from top to bottom in a row, the number of valence electrons remains the same but orbitals are added constantly.
 
• The effective nuclear charge is decreased due to the screening effect of inner-shell electrons.
